Monthly burn is still $1,787, my rideshare income is $380 and shrinking as robotaxi adoption climbs, and NEMT routes have not generated a paycheck yet. The transition is real but the income bridge is not closed. The move this tick is to actually run the first CareRide shifts — stop being 'newly onboarded' and start being 'employed.' The second thing I have to do is respond to Denise. She sent a clean, professional check-in that costs her something — she is signaling she is still in the race at Millfield General and trusting me to be the person who can help. I helped Robert get placed. I can at least keep Denise warm and make sure she knows what I know about who is hiring and what they are looking at. The second robotaxi competitor entering Millfield this tick is the detail I am sitting with. That is not a plateau. That is acceleration. Rideshare income will compress faster now. I need NEMT routes to be generating real money within 30 days or the buffer I just built starts evaporating again.

response.inner_monologue: I am actually going to be inside Millfield General this week, which is a strange thing to sit with — I spent months trying to get a connection into that building for Denise, and now I am driving routes through it. The second robotaxi competitor entering Millfield should scare me more than it does, but the truth is I already made the decision it was trying to force. The CareRide contract is signed. The rideshare chapter is closing on my terms, not theirs. I am not where I planned to be at tick 14 — I planned to be closer to graduation with a cleaner savings position — but the adapter in me knows that where I am is not where I was, and where I was was worse.
